Question B-003-021-009.

Why the correct answer is right: Indoor antennas should be kept as far as practical from occupied living spaces so distance reduces RF exposure to people in the home.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Position the antennas parallel to electrical power wires to take advantage of parasitic effects": Coupling to power wiring can create interference and safety problems; it is not an RF exposure precaution.
- sourceIndex 2: "Position the antennas along the edge of a wall where it meets the floor or ceiling to reduce parasitic radiation": A wall edge does not guarantee reduced radiation or safe separation from occupants.
- sourceIndex 3: "Locate the antennas close to your operating position to minimize transmission line length": Short coax may reduce loss, but putting the antenna close to the operator increases exposure instead of reducing it.
